correctness.rationale: The planar segment projection has complete, explicitly checked endpoint and interior optimality conditions. Strict coordinate separation excludes zero-coordinate projections under δ<min(a,b)/2; the positive distance to the true segment excludes p=0 and a homotopy fixes the signs. At the boundary the supplied rational endpoint witness has a zero true directional derivative; for every larger δ a negative-coordinate endpoint witness exists. Shared errors translate the segment, so a positive supporting line and endpoint conditions prove safety below ab/sqrt(a²+b²); the shifted original foot gives exact boundary and strict failure above. The code in verify.py executed with 12983 exact-rational cases, independent of universal proof.

originality.rationale: The two exact worst-case componentwise-error thresholds concern true common-descent preservation of the Euclidean projection onto a *noisy segment*. The source 2026 FMOO work defines the server projection but only analyzes expected Pareto-stationarity, while 2026 regularity-aware MGDA obtains direction-norm Hölder/Lipschitz estimates but not sharp sign-preservation radii nor the shared-error enlargement. Classical MGDA exact-gradient descent does not imply the perturbed result without further argument. Actual semantic record and literature queries found nearby algorithms and direction continuity results, not the same pair of sharp constants. Remaining priority risk is acknowledged.
residual_risks: Older work on inexact multiobjective steepest descent or projection perturbations may contain an equivalent two-gradient planar sharpness result under different terminology.

value.rationale: The server minimum-norm multi-gradient rule is used with objective-wise stochastic estimates, where cross-task dependence can matter. This theorem gives exact worst-case safe error budgets for the same pair of objective gradients under arbitrary versus identical vector errors, with an achieved and nontrivial ratio from √2 to 2. This is a mathematically natural structural comparison, rather than a mere numerical table or algorithm restatement; sharp counterexamples distinguish non-descent from ascent. It does not claim global optimization improvements.
